chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My Honour, and My Majesty, and My Magnificence, and My Glory, and the loftiness of My Exaltedness! No believing servant would prefer My desires over his own desires in anything from the matters of the world, except that I shall make richness to be in his soul, and concern him regarding his Hereafter, and I shall guarantee the skies and the earth for his sustenance, and I shall be for him behind the trade of every trader.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and material rewards for a believer who prioritizes God's will over their own desires?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith qudsi from al-Kafi underscores the concept of 'Ghina' (spiritual self-sufficiency) as a divine reward for prioritizing God's will over worldly desires. It highlights the metaphysical guarantee of rizq (sustenance) by the cosmos, positioning God as the ultimate guarantor of the believer's spiritual 'trade,' thereby linking asceticism with divine provision.
